questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A block of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is resting on an inclined plane of angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ as illustrated below. If the coefficient of static friction is $\mu_s = 0.6$, determine the minimum external horizontal force $F$ required to initiate upward motion along the incline. (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$).

questionImage.data: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 500 320" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"><rect width="500" height="320" fill="#F8FAFC" rx="16"/><polygon points="60,260 440,260 440,80" fill="#E2E8F0" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M 140,260 A 80 80 0 0 0 130,225" fill="none" stroke="#2563EB" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="248" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">θ = 30°</text><g transform="translate(250, 165) rotate(-26.5)"><rect x="-40" y="-40" width="80" height="40" fill="#3B82F6" stroke="#1D4ED8" stroke-width="2" rx="4"/><text x="-8" y="-15" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#FFFFFF">m</text><line x1="40" y1="-20" x2="100" y2="-20" stroke="#EF4444" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/><text x="108" y="-15" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#DC2626">F</text></g><defs><marker id="arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M 0 1 L 10 5 L 0 9 z" fill="#EF4444"/></marker></defs></svg>

questions.explanation:
Resolving forces along and perpendicular to the incline:
$$N = mg\cos\theta + F\sin\theta$$
To move up: $F\cos\theta = mg\sin\theta + f_s^{\max} = mg\sin\theta + \mu_s N$.
Substituting $\theta = 30^\circ$ and $\mu_s = 0.6$ yields $F \approx 23.4\text{ N}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A conservative particle moves along the x-axis with potential energy function $U(x) = \alpha x^4 - \beta x^2$, where $\alpha = 1\text{ J/m}^4$ and $\beta = 8\text{ J/m}^2$. The non-zero stable equilibrium positions of the particle are located at:
questions.explanation:
For equilibrium, $\frac{dU}{dx} = 0 \implies 4\alpha x^3 - 2\beta x = 0$.
$x(4x^2 - 16) = 0 \implies x = 0$ or $x = \pm 2\text{ m}$.
Evaluating $\frac{d^2U}{dx^2} = 12x^2 - 16$ at $x = \pm 2$: $12(4) - 16 = 32 > 0$ (Stable minimum).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the bridge network shown below, calculate the equivalent resistance $R_{AB}$ across terminals A and B if all five resistors have identical resistance $R = 10\,\Omega$.

questionImage.data: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 460 260" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"><rect width="460" height="260" fill="#F8FAFC" rx="14"/><circle cx="40" cy="130" r="6" fill="#2563EB"/><text x="20" y="135" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">A</text><circle cx="420" cy="130" r="6" fill="#2563EB"/><text x="432" y="135" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E40AF">B</text><line x1="40" y1="130" x2="100" y2="130" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="2.5"/><polygon points="100,130 230,40 360,130 230,220" fill="none" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="230" y1="40" x2="230" y2="220" stroke="#E11D48" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="360" y1="130" x2="420" y2="130" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="145" y="75" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#0F172A">10 Ω</text><text x="295" y="75" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#0F172A">10 Ω</text><text x="145" y="195" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#0F172A">10 Ω</text><text x="295" y="195" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#0F172A">10 Ω</text><text x="238" y="135" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#BE123C">10 Ω</text></svg>

questions.explanation:
Because $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{R_3}{R_4} = \frac{10}{10} = 1$, the bridge is balanced.
No current flows through the central branch.
$R_{AB} = (10 + 10) \parallel (10 + 10) = 20 \parallel 20 = 10\,\Omega$.
